title: From an overcounting dichotomy to a base-p digit criterion
content: The parent proved that over a characteristic-p field the ordinary iterated-derivative multiplicity test is exact for true multiplicity m < p and blind for m ≥ p, and asked to stratify the unbounded regime by the base-p digits of m via the Lucas/Kummer structure of the binomials C(m,k) defining hasseDeriv. This entry answers it for the pure power Xᵐ: hasseDeriv k (Xᵐ) is a single monomial C(m,k)·X^(m-k), so it survives over characteristic p exactly when p ∤ C(m,k), and Lucas's theorem turns that into the carry-free digit-domination condition on k and m.
mathContext: $\mathrm{hasseDeriv}_k(X^m) = \binom{m}{k} X^{m-k}$; over $\mathrm{char}\,p$ it is nonzero $\iff p \nmid \binom{m}{k} \iff$ every base-$p$ digit of $k$ is $\le$ that of $m$.

title: The Hasse derivative of a pure power is a single monomial
content: hasseDeriv_X_pow: writing Xᵐ = monomial m 1 and applying hasseDeriv_monomial gives hasseDeriv k (Xᵐ) = C(m,k)·X^(m-k). Because this is a single monomial, over a field it vanishes iff its coefficient does; combined with CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff this yields hasseDeriv_X_pow_ne_zero_iff: hasseDeriv k (Xᵐ) ≠ 0 ↔ ¬ p ∣ C(m,k). This is the bridge that converts the polynomial survival question into a divisibility question about binomials.
mathContext: $\mathrm{hasseDeriv}_k(X^m) = \binom{m}{k} X^{m-k}$; over a field $\mathrm{monomial}\,(m-k)\,c = 0 \iff c = 0$, and $(\binom{m}{k} : F) = 0 \iff p \mid \binom{m}{k}$.

title: The single-digit Lucas building block
content: not_dvd_choose_digit_iff: for one base-p digit position, i.e. a < p, the binomial C(a,b) avoids p exactly when b ≤ a. If b > a the binomial is 0 (hence divisible); if b ≤ a < p, then from C(a,b)·b!·(a-b)! = a! and p ∤ a! (because a < p, via Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial) we get p ∤ C(a,b). Multiplied across digits by Lucas's theorem, this becomes the full digit-domination criterion.
mathContext: For $a < p$ prime: $p \nmid \binom{a}{b} \iff b \le a$, since $\binom{a}{b}\,b!\,(a-b)! = a!$ and $p \nmid a!$.

title: Capstone: the Lucas digit-domination criterion
content: hasseDeriv_X_pow_ne_zero_iff_digits: for m,k < p^a over a characteristic-p field, hasseDeriv k (Xᵐ) ≠ 0 iff every base-p digit of k is dominated by the corresponding digit of m. The proof feeds Mathlib's Lucas congruence C(m,k) ≡ ∏ C(mᵢ,kᵢ) mod p, transfers divisibility across it (Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd), reduces the product to a single factor (Prime.dvd_finset_prod_iff), and applies the single-digit criterion. This is exactly the requested stratification: the ordinary test reads only k < p, but the surviving Hasse orders are the digit-dominated k, reaching k = m once m ≥ p.
mathContext: $\mathrm{hasseDeriv}_k(X^m) \ne 0 \iff \forall i < a,\ \lfloor k/p^i \rfloor \bmod p \le \lfloor m/p^i \rfloor \bmod p$ (Kummer: the sum $k + (m-k)$ has no base-$p$ carries).

title: The digit count ∏(dᵢ+1) realized over 𝔽₂
content: The count of surviving orders equals ∏(dᵢ+1) over the base-p digits dᵢ of m (Glaisher/Fine — the number of odd binomials in row m of Pascal's triangle over 𝔽₂). nonzero_orders_X3_F2: X³ has digits 11₂, so all four orders k ≤ 3 survive (2·2 = 4). nonzero_orders_X4_F2: X⁴ has digits 100₂, so only k ∈ {0,4} survive (1·1·2 = 2). hasseDeriv_X4_F2_profile states directly that k = 1,2,3 vanish while k = 0,4 survive. All by `decide` (kernel), not native_decide, keeping the file 0-axiom.
mathContext: Row 3 of Pascal mod 2: $1,1,1,1$ (all odd) $\Rightarrow 4$ survivors; row 4: $1,0,0,0,1 \Rightarrow 2$ survivors. Both equal $\prod (d_i + 1)$.
